title: Pay now, terms later and rolling formation
summary: Rolling formation describes an approach in which a seller supplies detailed terms with a product and invites acceptance by retaining or using it after an opportunity to review and return it.
notes:
Hill accepts that account of the transaction and treats retention beyond the specified period as acceptance. Klocek instead treats the consumer as having made an offer that the seller already accepted, so the box terms require a separate basis for inclusion. The disagreement concerns who made the offer, when the contract formed, what notice was provided, and whether § 2-207 applies. A return period is a relevant fact; it does not automatically resolve every transaction involving later terms.

Hill uses retention after a review-and-return period to complete the vendor’s offer and treats the one-form transaction outside § 2-207. Klocek finds no textual two-form prerequisite and, on its evidentiary record, assumes the consumer made the offer and the vendor accepted earlier. The differences include governing law, procedural posture, notice, and offeror identity as well as the length of the return period. The notes retain later developments as dated reports.
